 --> PM Modi visit: Bengaluru traffic police issue advisory; schools announce holiday in parts of city
 Traffic restrictions will be imposed across south Bengaluru on November 13 during the Prime Minister’s visit and inauguration of the Namma Metro Pink Line. Several schools have suspended classes, citing traffic diversions and possible congestion. 
 Moneycontrol News 
 November 12, 2026 / 17:54 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 X/@ishanjain28 
 Bengaluru traffic police have issued an advisory ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the city on November 13, announcing temporary traffic restrictions and diversions across several parts of south Bengaluru.
 Meanwhile, Bannerghatta Road is being spruced up ahead of the Prime Minister’s visit. Several schools in south Bengaluru have also announced a holiday for Friday, anticipating traffic diversions and congestion.
 The restrictions will be imposed during VVIP movement and at locations where programmes are scheduled. Areas under Adugodi, Jayanagar, JP Nagar, Thalaghattapura, Hulimavu and Mico Layout traffic police stations will be affected, a statement said.
 Motorists travelling towards Jayadeva Hospital, Dairy Circle, Bannerghatta Road and surrounding areas have been advised to plan their journeys and use alternative routes, it said.
 Bannerghatta Road, Dairy Circle restrictions

 Under Adugodi traffic police limits, vehicles travelling from Anepalya Junction towards Jayadeva Hospital via Dairy Circle will face restrictions near Micobande Junction and the Dairy Circle underpass. Motorists can take a right turn at Micobande Junction, proceed along New Micobande Road towards Adugodi Junction and then take a right turn towards Hosur Laskar Main Road.
 Alternatively, commuters can use BG Road and the Dairy Circle service road to reach Dr Marigowda Road, Madiwala Check Post and Hosur Road. Restrictions will also be imposed on Bannerghatta Road between Dairy Circle Junction and Arekere Junction during VVIP movement.
 Restrictions in Jayanagar, JP Nagar 
 Under Jayanagar traffic police limits, vehicles travelling from Marenahalli Main Road towards Jayadeva Hospital Junction via 28th Main Road will face restrictions.
 Traffic from East End Junction towards Bannerghatta Road via Swagath Junction will also be affected.
 Motorists travelling from Banashankari towards Silk Board can use the Ragigudda double-decker road, except during VVIP movement. Commuters from East End Junction can take 28th Main Road and East End Road to reach Swagath Road and JP Nagar Dalmia Junction.
 In JP Nagar, restrictions will be imposed on the Outer Ring Road stretch between 15th Cross and 24th Main Road Junction, and at JD Mara Junction on Bannerghatta Road. Traffic will also be restricted from RV Dental Junction towards Bannerghatta Main Road and on BPL Arekere Main Road.
 Motorists heading towards Hosur Road can use Kanakapura Main Road, Banashankari Bus Stand and 46th Cross Road. Those travelling towards Bannerghatta Road can take Kanakapura Main Road and turn at Konanakunte Cross or A2B Junction.
 Diversions in Thalaghattapura, Hulimavu 
 Vehicles travelling from Anjanapura 80 Feet Road towards Bannerghatta Road will face restrictions. Traffic near Gottigere Lake, Karnataka Bank and Loyola School will also be affected.
 Motorists from Anjanapura can use the route via BMTC Depot, Tulasipura Fire Station, Lal Bahadur Shastri Nagar and Kanakapura Road.
 In Hulimavu, restrictions will affect vehicles travelling from Bannerghatta Main Road towards Arekere, Bilekahalli, Mico Layout, Dairy Circle and the city.
 Alternative routes include Koli Farm Gate Junction via CK Palya Junction and Begur-Koppa Road, Sherwood Junction via NICE Road, and BDA Junction via Anjanapura 80 Feet Road.
 Parking restrictions; schools announce holiday 
 Traffic police have prohibited parking on several roads, including 8th Main Road in JP Nagar 2nd Phase, 15th Cross Road between Dalmia Junction and Bannerghatta Main Road, Marenahalli Main Road, East End Main Road, Swagath Main Road and 28th Main Road.
 Meanwhile, some schools in south Bengaluru have announced a holiday on Friday, citing anticipated traffic diversions and congestion due to the Prime Minister’s visit.
 In a communication to parents, a school on Bannerghatta Road said classes from pre-primary to Class 12 would remain suspended on November 13 to ensure student safety and avoid transportation-related inconvenience.
 PM to inaugurate projects worth Rs 15,600 crore 
 PM Modi is scheduled to participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram at around 10:45 am. At around 12:45 pm, he will flag off and undertake a Metro ride from Tavarekere to IIM Bangalore station.
 He will subsequently inaugurate, dedicate to the nation and lay the foundation stones for development projects worth more than Rs 15,600 crore.
 The key projects include the inauguration of Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere, developed at a cost of around Rs 3,470 crore.
 Other projects include renewable energy transmission infrastructure in Koppal, Gadag and Bidar, a compressed biogas plant in Bengaluru, and the inauguration of four redeveloped railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.
 PM Modi will also flag off the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express and dedicate the electrification of the Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road railway section.
 The Prime Minister will travel to Mysuru later in the day to inaugurate COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, India's first LED dome planetarium.
